**Tafsir Surat al-Hujurat**
It is a Medinan surah. [[In A: "It is Medinan, eighteen verses."]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

These are etiquettes (ādāb) with which Allah taught His believing servants how to conduct themselves toward the Messenger (ﷺ), in reverence, respect, honour and glorification. He says: ﴿O you who have believed, do not put yourselves forward before Allah and His Messenger [and fear Allah]﴾. [[Addition from M.]] That is: do not be hasty in matters before him, that is, ahead of him. Rather, follow him in all affairs, so that the hadith of Mu'adh enters within the generality of this legislated etiquette, when the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him when he sent him to Yemen: "By what will you judge?" He said: "By the Book of Allah." He said: "And if you do not find it?" He said: "By the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah." He said: "And if you do not find it?" He said: "I will exert my opinion (ajtahidu ra'yī)." So he struck his chest and said: "Praise be to Allah who has granted success to the messenger of the Messenger of Allah, to what pleases the Messenger of Allah."

It was narrated by Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah. [[Previously discussed in the introduction to the book.]] The point of it is that he deferred his opinion, reasoning and effort until after the Book and the Sunnah. Had he put it forward before searching in them, it would have been a case of putting oneself forward before Allah and His Messenger.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning ﴿Do not put yourselves forward before Allah and His Messenger﴾: "Do not say anything contrary to the Book and the Sunnah."

al-'Awfi narrated from him: "They were forbidden to speak before his speech."

Mujahid said: "Do not presume anything against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) until Allah decides it upon his tongue."

al-Dahhak said: "Do not decide any matter apart from Allah and His Messenger from among the laws of your religion."

Sufyan al-Thawri said concerning ﴿Do not put yourselves forward before Allah and His Messenger﴾: "by speech or by action."

al-Hasan al-Basri said concerning ﴿Do not put yourselves forward before Allah and His Messenger﴾: "Do not make supplication before the imam."

Qatadah said: "It was mentioned to us that some people used to say: 'If only such-and-such were revealed concerning such-and-such, or if only such-and-such were done,' so Allah disliked that, and it has preceded."

﴿And fear Allah﴾, that is, regarding what He has commanded you. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Hearing﴾, that is, of your statements, ﴿Knowing﴾ of your intentions.

* *

His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet﴾. This is a second etiquette with which Allah taught the believers: that they should not raise their voices in the presence of the Prophet (ﷺ) [above his voice]. [[Addition from T, M, A.]] It has been narrated that this was revealed concerning the two sheikhs, Abu Bakr and 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both.

al-Bukhari said: Busrah ibn Safwan al-Lakhmi narrated to us, Nafi' ibn 'Umar narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, who said: "The two good ones nearly perished, Abu Bakr and 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, when they raised their voices in the presence of the Prophet (ﷺ) when a delegation of Banu Tamim arrived at him. One of them pointed to al-Aqra' ibn Habis, brother of Banu Mujashi', and the other pointed to another man." (Nafi' said: "I do not remember his name.") Abu Bakr said to 'Umar: "You only intended to oppose me." He said: "I did not intend to oppose you." So their voices were raised over that, and Allah revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet and do not speak loudly to him as you speak loudly to one another﴾, to the end of the verse. Ibn al-Zubayr said: "After this verse, 'Umar would not speak to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) without asking him in a low voice, and he did not mention that about his father, meaning Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him." He was alone in narrating it, apart from Muslim. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4845).]]

Then al-Bukhari said: Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abi Mulaykah told me that 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr informed him that a delegation of Banu Tamim came to the Prophet (ﷺ). Abu Bakr said: "Appoint al-Qa'qa' ibn Ma'bad." 'Umar said: "Rather, appoint al-Aqra' ibn Habis." Abu Bakr said: "You only intended to oppose me," or "except to oppose me." 'Umar said: "I did not intend to oppose you." He narrated it likewise here, alone as well. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4847).]]

The memorizer (al-Hafiz) Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said in his Musnad: Al-Fadl ibn Sahl narrated to us, Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to us, Husayn ibn 'Umar narrated to us, from Mukhariq, from Tariq ibn Shihab, from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, who said: "When this verse was revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet﴾, I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I will not speak to you except as a brother speaks in confidence.'" [[Musnad al-Bazzar, no. (2257), "Kashf al-Astar." He said: "We do not know it to be narrated connected except from Abu Bakr, and Husayn narrated hadiths that no one followed him in, Mukhariq is well known, and the rest are reliable."]]

This Husayn ibn 'Umar, although he is weak, we have narrated something similar from the hadith of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf and Abu Hurayrah [may Allah be pleased with him]. [[Addition from A.]] And Allah knows best. [[As for the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak (2/462) through Muhammad ibn 'Amr from Abu Salamah from him, and said: "Its isnad is sahih according to the condition of Muslim, though they did not record it," and al-Dhahabi agreed.]]

al-Bukhari said: 'Ali ibn 'Abdullah narrated to us, Azhar ibn Sa'd narrated to us, Ibn 'Awn informed us, Musa ibn Anas told me, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) missed Thabit ibn Qays. A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, I will find out his news for you." So he went to him and found him in his house with his head bowed. He said to him: "What is the matter with you?" He said: "Evil. He used to raise his voice above the voice of the Prophet (ﷺ), so his deeds have been nullified, and he is among the people of the Fire." The man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him that he had said such and such. Musa said: "So he returned to him the second time with a great glad tiding and said: 'Go to him and say: You are not among the people of the Fire, but you are among the people of Paradise.'" Al-Bukhari alone narrated it by this route. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4846).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Hashim narrated to us, Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas, who said: "When this verse was revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet﴾ up to ﴿while you do not perceive﴾, Thabit ibn Qays ibn al-Shammas had a loud voice. He said: 'I am the one who used to raise my voice over the voice of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). My deeds have been nullified; I am among the people of the Fire.' He sat in his household, grieving. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) missed him, so some of the people went to him and said: 'The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has missed you; what is the matter with you?' He said: 'I am the one who raises my voice above the voice of the Prophet (ﷺ), and I speak loudly to him; my deeds have been nullified; I am among the people of the Fire.' They came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him of what he had said. He said: 'No, rather he is among the people of Paradise.'" Anas said: "We used to see him walking among us, and we knew that he was among the people of Paradise. When the day of al-Yamamah came, some of us were routed. Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas came, having applied perfume and put on his shroud, and said: 'How evil is what you accustom your companions to.' He fought them until he was killed." [[In T: "until he was killed, may Allah have mercy on him."]] [[Al-Musnad (3/137).]]

Muslim said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn Musa narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Thabit al-Bunani, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: "When this verse was revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet﴾ to the end of the verse, Thabit sat in his house and said: 'I am among the people of the Fire.' He withdrew from the Prophet (ﷺ). The Prophet (ﷺ) asked Sa'd ibn Mu'adh: 'O Abu 'Amr, what is the matter with Thabit? Is he ill?' Sa'd said: 'He is my neighbour, and I know of no complaint from him.' So Sa'd came to him and mentioned to him the statement of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Thabit said: 'This verse was revealed, and you know that I am among the loudest of you in voice over the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so I am among the people of the Fire.' Sa'd mentioned that to the Prophet (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Rather, he is among the people of Paradise.'"

Then Muslim narrated it from Ahmad ibn Sa'id al-Darimi, from Hayyan ibn Hilal, from Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah, with the same, and he said: "He did not mention Sa'd ibn Mu'adh." And from Qatan ibn Nusayr, from Ja'far ibn Sulayman, from Thabit, from Anas, something similar, and he said: "There is no mention of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh in it."

Hurayim ibn 'Abd al-A'la al-Asadi narrated to us, al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, "I heard my father mention, from Thabit, from Anas, who said: 'When this verse was revealed,'" and he recounted the hadith, not mentioning Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, and added: "So we used to see him walking among us, a man of the people of Paradise." [[Sahih Muslim, no. (119).]]

These three routes point to the weakness of Hammad ibn Salamah's narration in what he alone reported, namely the mention of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh. The correct view is that at the time this verse was revealed, Sa'd ibn Mu'adh was not present, for he died a few days after Banu Qurayzah in the fifth year (AH), whereas this verse was revealed concerning the delegation of Banu Tamim, and delegations came in large numbers only in the ninth year of the Hijrah. And Allah knows best.

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrated to us, Abu Thabit ibn Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas narrated to us, my paternal uncle Isma'il ibn Muhammad ibn Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas told me, from his father, who said: "When this verse was revealed: ﴿Do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet and do not speak loudly to him﴾, Thabit ibn Qays [ibn Shammas] sat on the road weeping. 'Asim ibn 'Adi of Banu al-'Ajlan passed by him and said: 'What makes you weep, O Thabit?' He said: 'This verse. I fear that it was revealed concerning me, for I am loud-voiced and high-pitched.'" He said: "'Asim went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he was overcome by weeping. He came to his wife Jamilah, daughter of 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, and said to her: 'When I enter the stable of my horse, fasten the iron ring on me with a nail.' She struck it with a nail until, when he came out, he pulled it back and said: 'I will not come out until Allah, Mighty and Majestic, takes me, or the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is pleased with me.'" He said: "'Asim came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and informed him of his news. He said: 'Go and call him to me.' 'Asim came to the place and did not find him, so he went to his family and found him in the stable. He said to him: 'The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is calling you.' He said: 'Break the ring.' They went out and came to the Prophet (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: 'What makes you weep, O Thabit?' He said: 'I am loud-voiced, and I fear that this verse was revealed concerning me: ﴿Do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet and do not speak loudly to him﴾.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: 'Are you not content to live praiseworthy, to be killed as a martyr, and to enter Paradise?' He said: 'I am content with the glad tidings of Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ), and I will never raise my voice again above the voice of the Prophet (ﷺ).'" He said: "And Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, those who lower their voices in the presence of the Messenger of Allah are those whose hearts Allah has tested for piety﴾ [[In A, after it: "For them is forgiveness and a great reward," in place of "the verse."]]. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (26/75).]]

Also, a number of the Successors (tabi'un) have related this story in the same way. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, forbade raising the voice in the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. We have also related from the Commander of the Faithful, 'Umar ibn al-Khattab [may Allah be pleased with him] [[Addition from T.]] that he heard the voices of two men in the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah [[In T and M: "the Prophet".]] ﷺ raised high, so he came and said: "Do you know where you are?" Then he said: "Where are you from?" They said: "From the people of Ta'if." He said: "If you were from the people of Madinah, I would have beaten you severely." [[Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (470), by way of al-Sa'ib ibn Yazid, and he mentioned it.]]

The scholars said: Raising the voice at his grave is disliked, just as it was disliked during his lifetime, because he is honored both while alive and in his grave, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him [[In T: "may Allah bless him and grant him peace".]], always. Then He forbade speaking to him loudly, as a man speaks loudly to one he addresses from among others; rather, he should be addressed with tranquility, dignity and reverence. For this reason He said: ﴿And do not speak loudly to him as you speak loudly to one another﴾, just as He said: ﴿Do not make the call of the Messenger among yourselves like the call of some of you to others﴾ [An-Nur: 63].

* *

And His saying: ﴿lest your deeds be nullified while you perceive not﴾ means: We only forbade you from raising your voices in his presence out of fear that he would become angry at that, and then Allah would become angry on account of his anger, and Allah would nullify the deeds of the one who angered him while he is unaware, as it came in the Sahih: "Indeed a man may speak a word of Allah's pleasure, giving it no thought, and it raises him in rank by it; and indeed a man may speak a word of Allah's displeasure, giving it no thought, and it casts him into Hell further than the distance between the heavens and the earth." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (6478), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic [[In T: "glorified and exalted is He".]], encouraged lowering the voice in his presence, urged it, guided to it, and made it desirable, saying: ﴿Indeed, those who lower their voices in the presence of the Messenger of Allah—those are the ones whose hearts Allah has tested for piety﴾, meaning: He purified them for it and made them fit and a place for it. ﴿For them is forgiveness and a great reward﴾.

Imam Ahmad related in Kitab al-Zuhd: Abd al-Rahman related to us, Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, who said: A letter was written to 'Umar [[In T: "'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him".]]: "O Commander of the Faithful, a man who does not desire sin and does not act upon it—is he better, or a man who desires sin but does not act upon it?" So 'Umar wrote, may Allah be pleased with him: "Indeed, those who desire sin but do not act upon it—﴿those are the ones whose hearts Allah has tested for piety; for them is forgiveness and a great reward﴾." [[Mentioned by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (7/552) and attributed it to Ahmad in al-Zuhd.]]

**Tafsir Surat al-Hujurat**
It is a Medinan surah. [[In A: "It is Medinan, eighteen verses."]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

These are etiquettes (ādāb) with which Allah taught His believing servants how to conduct themselves toward the Messenger (ﷺ), in reverence, respect, honour and glorification. He says: ﴿O you who have believed, do not put yourselves forward before Allah and His Messenger [and fear Allah]﴾. [[Addition from M.]] That is: do not be hasty in matters before him, that is, ahead of him. Rather, follow him in all affairs, so that the hadith of Mu'adh enters within the generality of this legislated etiquette, when the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him when he sent him to Yemen: "By what will you judge?" He said: "By the Book of Allah." He said: "And if you do not find it?" He said: "By the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah." He said: "And if you do not find it?" He said: "I will exert my opinion (ajtahidu ra'yī)." So he struck his chest and said: "Praise be to Allah who has granted success to the messenger of the Messenger of Allah, to what pleases the Messenger of Allah."

It was narrated by Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah. [[Previously discussed in the introduction to the book.]] The point of it is that he deferred his opinion, reasoning and effort until after the Book and the Sunnah. Had he put it forward before searching in them, it would have been a case of putting oneself forward before Allah and His Messenger.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning ﴿Do not put yourselves forward before Allah and His Messenger﴾: "Do not say anything contrary to the Book and the Sunnah."

al-'Awfi narrated from him: "They were forbidden to speak before his speech."

Mujahid said: "Do not presume anything against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) until Allah decides it upon his tongue."

al-Dahhak said: "Do not decide any matter apart from Allah and His Messenger from among the laws of your religion."

Sufyan al-Thawri said concerning ﴿Do not put yourselves forward before Allah and His Messenger﴾: "by speech or by action."

al-Hasan al-Basri said concerning ﴿Do not put yourselves forward before Allah and His Messenger﴾: "Do not make supplication before the imam."

Qatadah said: "It was mentioned to us that some people used to say: 'If only such-and-such were revealed concerning such-and-such, or if only such-and-such were done,' so Allah disliked that, and it has preceded."

﴿And fear Allah﴾, that is, regarding what He has commanded you. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Hearing﴾, that is, of your statements, ﴿Knowing﴾ of your intentions.

* *

His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet﴾. This is a second etiquette with which Allah taught the believers: that they should not raise their voices in the presence of the Prophet (ﷺ) [above his voice]. [[Addition from T, M, A.]] It has been narrated that this was revealed concerning the two sheikhs, Abu Bakr and 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both.

One of them pointed to al-Aqra' ibn Habis, brother of Banu Mujashi', and the other pointed to another man." (Nafi' said: "I do not remember his name.") Abu Bakr said to 'Umar: "You only intended to oppose me." He said: "I did not intend to oppose you." So their voices were raised over that, and Allah revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet and do not speak loudly to him as you speak loudly to one another﴾, to the end of the verse. Ibn al-Zubayr said: "After this verse, 'Umar would not speak to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) without asking him in a low voice, and he did not mention that about his father, meaning Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him." He was alone in narrating it, apart from Muslim. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4845).]]

Then al-Bukhari said: Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abi Mulaykah told me that 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr informed him that a delegation of Banu Tamim came to the Prophet (ﷺ). Abu Bakr said: "Appoint al-Qa'qa' ibn Ma'bad." 'Umar said: "Rather, appoint al-Aqra' ibn Habis." Abu Bakr said: "You only intended to oppose me," or "except to oppose me." 'Umar said: "I did not intend to oppose you." So they disputed until their voices were raised, and concerning that this was revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not put yourselves forward before Allah and His Messenger﴾, until the end of the verse, ﴿And if they had patiently waited until you came out to them...﴾ to the end of the verse. [al-Hujurat: 5]

He narrated it likewise here, alone as well. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4847).]]

The memorizer (al-Hafiz) Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said in his Musnad: Al-Fadl ibn Sahl narrated to us, Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to us, Husayn ibn 'Umar narrated to us, from Mukhariq, from Tariq ibn Shihab, from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, who said: "When this verse was revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet﴾, I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I will not speak to you except as a brother speaks in confidence.'" [[Musnad al-Bazzar, no. (2257), "Kashf al-Astar." This Husayn ibn 'Umar, although he is weak, we have narrated something similar from the hadith of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf and Abu Hurayrah [may Allah be pleased with him]. [[Addition from A.]] And Allah knows best. [[As for the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak (2/462) through Muhammad ibn 'Amr from Abu Salamah from him, and said: "Its isnad is sahih according to the condition of Muslim, though they did not record it," and al-Dhahabi agreed.]]

al-Bukhari said: 'Ali ibn 'Abdullah narrated to us, Azhar ibn Sa'd narrated to us, Ibn 'Awn informed us, Musa ibn Anas told me, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) missed Thabit ibn Qays. A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, I will find out his news for you." So he went to him and found him in his house with his head bowed. He said to him: "What is the matter with you?" He said: "Evil. He used to raise his voice above the voice of the Prophet (ﷺ), so his deeds have been nullified, and he is among the people of the Fire." The man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him that he had said such and such. Musa said: "So he returned to him the second time with a great glad tiding and said: 'Go to him and say: You are not among the people of the Fire, but you are among the people of Paradise.'" [[In T: "until he was killed, may Allah have mercy on him."]] [[Al-Musnad (3/137).]]

He withdrew from the Prophet (ﷺ). The Prophet (ﷺ) asked Sa'd ibn Mu'adh: 'O Abu 'Amr, what is the matter with Thabit? Is he ill?' Sa'd said: 'He is my neighbour, and I know of no complaint from him.' So Sa'd came to him and mentioned to him the statement of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Thabit said: 'This verse was revealed, and you know that I am among the loudest of you in voice over the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so I am among the people of the Fire.' Sa'd mentioned that to the Prophet (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Rather, he is among the people of Paradise.'"

Then Muslim narrated it from Ahmad ibn Sa'id al-Darimi, from Hayyan ibn Hilal, from Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah, with the same, and he said: "He did not mention Sa'd ibn Mu'adh." And from Qatan ibn Nusayr, from Ja'far ibn Sulayman, from Thabit, from Anas, something similar, and he said: "There is no mention of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh in it."

[[Sahih Muslim, no. (119).]]

O Allah, I ask You for everlasting bliss that does not change and does not vanish. O Allah, I ask You for bliss on the day of need, and security on the day of fear. O Allah, I seek refuge with You from the evil of what You have given us and from the evil of what You have withheld from us. O Allah, make faith beloved to us and adorn it in our hearts, and make disbelief, defiance and disobedience hateful to us, and make us among the rightly guided. O Allah, cause us to die as Muslims, keep us alive as Muslims, and join us with the righteous, neither disgraced nor led into trial. So they stood in rows behind him, and he said: 'O Allah, all praise is Yours entirely. O Allah, there is none who can withhold what You have extended, and none who can extend what You have withheld. None can guide whom You have led astray, and none can lead astray whom You have guided. None can give what You have withheld, and none can withhold what You have given. None can bring near what You have put far, and none can put far what You have brought near. O Allah, extend upon us Your blessings, Your mercy, Your bounty and Your provision. O Allah, I ask You for everlasting bliss that does not change and does not vanish. O Allah, I ask You for bliss on the day of need, and security on the day of fear. O Allah, I seek refuge with You from the evil of what You have given us and from the evil of what You have withheld from us. O Allah, make faith beloved to us and adorn it in our hearts, and make disbelief, defiance and disobedience hateful to us, and make us among the rightly guided. O Allah, cause us to die as Muslims, keep us alive as Muslims, and join us with the righteous, neither disgraced nor led into trial. O Allah, fight the disbelievers who deny Your messengers and turn people away from Your way, and bring upon them Your punishment and Your torment. O Allah, fight the disbelievers who were given the Book, O God of truth.'"

It was also narrated by al-Nasa'i in Al-Yawm wa al-Layla, from Ziyad ibn Ayyub, from Marwan ibn Mu'awiya, from Abd al-Wahid ibn Ayman, from Ubayd ibn Rifa'a, from his father, with the same wording [[Al-Musnad (3/424) and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. (10445).]].

Then He said: ﴿As a bounty from Allah and a favor﴾, meaning: this bestowal which He has granted you [[In T: "al-qada'" (the decree).]] is a bounty from Him upon you and a favor from His presence, ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾, meaning: He knows who deserves guidance and who deserves misguidance, and He is wise in His sayings and His actions, and in His legislation and His decree.

The Almighty commands that the report of a wrongdoer (fasiq) be verified, so that caution is exercised regarding it, lest a judgment be passed on the basis of his word, when in reality it is false or mistaken. The one who judges by his word has then followed it blindly, and Allah has forbidden following the way of the corrupters. For this reason, some scholars refrained from accepting the narration of a person whose condition is unknown (majhul al-hal), given the possibility that he is a wrongdoer in reality. Others accepted it, because we were only commanded to verify when the report comes from a wrongdoer, and this person is not definitively known to be a wrongdoer, since his condition is unknown. We have settled this question in the Book of Knowledge in our commentary on al-Bukhari, and to Allah belongs all praise and grace.

Many of the exegetes (mufassirun) have mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning al-Walid ibn 'Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent him to collect the charity (sadaqat) of the Banu al-Mustaliq. This has been related through several chains, and the best of them is what Imam Ahmad related in his Musnad through the narration of the king of the Banu al-Mustaliq, who was al-Harith ibn Dirar, the father of Juwayriyah bint al-Harith, the Mother of the Believers, may Allah be pleased with her. Imam Ahmad said:

"Muhammad ibn Sabiq related to us, 'Isa ibn Dinar related to us, my father related to me that he heard al-Harith ibn Dirar al-Khuza'i say: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he invited me to Islam, so I entered it and affirmed it. He invited me to zakat, and I affirmed it. I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I will return to my people and invite them to Islam and to paying zakat. Whoever responds to me, I will gather his zakat, and you send a messenger to me at such and such a time, so that he may come to you with what I have gathered of zakat.' When al-Harith had gathered the zakat from those who responded to him, and the time came that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had wanted to send to him, the messenger was delayed and did not come to him. Al-Harith thought that some displeasure (sukhtah) from Allah and His Messenger had occurred concerning him. So he summoned the chiefs of his people and said to them: 'The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had set a time for me, when he would send his messenger to collect what I had of zakat. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ does not break promises, and I do not think his messenger was held back except because of some displeasure. So let us set out and go to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent al-Walid ibn 'Uqbah to al-Harith to collect what he had of the zakat he had gathered. When al-Walid had traveled until he reached part of the road, he became frightened (faraqa, i.e., feared) and returned and came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, al-Harith withheld zakat from me and wanted to kill me.' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then dispatched a force to al-Harith. Al-Harith set out with his companions, and when the force approached and departed from Medina, al-Harith met them. They said: 'This is al-Harith.' When he came upon them, he said to them: 'To whom have you been sent?' They said: 'To you.' He said: 'Why?' They said: 'The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had sent al-Walid ibn 'Uqbah to you, and he claimed that you withheld zakat from him and wanted to kill him.' He said: 'No, by the One who sent Muhammad with the truth, I did not see him at all, nor did he come to me.' When al-Harith entered upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he said: 'Did you withhold zakat and want to kill my messenger?' He said: 'No, by the One who sent you with the truth, I did not see him, nor did he come to me. I only came when the messenger of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was held back from me, and I feared that there had been some displeasure from Allah and His Messenger.'" He said: "Then the Surah al-Hujurat was revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, if a wrongdoer comes to you with a report, verify it﴾, up to His saying: ﴿Wise﴾."

Ibn Abi Hatim related it through al-Mundhir ibn Shadhan al-Tammar, from Muhammad ibn Sabiq with the same chain. al-Tabarani related it from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Sabiq with the same chain, except that he named him al-Harith ibn Sirar; the correct name is al-Harith ibn Dirar, as mentioned earlier.

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb related to us, Ja'far ibn 'Awn related to us, from Musa ibn 'Ubaydah, from Thabit, the freedman of Umm Salamah, from Umm Salamah, who said: "After the battle (al-waqi'ah), the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent a man to collect the charity of the Banu al-Mustaliq. The people heard of this, and they met him, showing great respect for the command of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. She said: Then Satan suggested to him that they intended to kill him. She said: So he returned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: 'The Banu al-Mustaliq have withheld their charity from me.' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the Muslims became angry. She said: The people learned of his return, so they came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and they lined up before him when he had prayed Dhuhr, and said: 'We seek refuge in Allah from the wrath of Allah and the wrath of His Messenger. You sent to us a man who collects charity, and we were delighted by that, and our eyes were gladdened. Then he returned from part of the way, and we feared that this was anger from Allah and from His Messenger.' They continued speaking to him until Bilal came and called the adhan for the 'Asr prayer." She said: "And this was revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, if a wrongdoer comes to you with a report, verify it, lest you harm a people in ignorance and then become regretful for what you have done﴾."

When the news reached them, they rejoiced and went out to meet the messenger of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When al-Walid was told that they had come out to meet him, he returned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, the Banu al-Mustaliq have withheld the charity.' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ became exceedingly angry at this. While he was pondering in himself whether to make war on them, the delegation came to him and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we were told that your messenger turned back halfway, and we feared that what turned him back was a letter that came from you because of anger you had toward us. We seek refuge in Allah from His anger and the anger of His Messenger.' The Prophet ﷺ tested them and was resolved against them, so Allah revealed their excuse in the Book, saying: ﴿O you who have believed, if a wrongdoer comes to you with a report, verify it﴾, to the end of the verse."

Mujahid and Qatadah said: "The Messenger of Allah sent al-Walid ibn 'Uqbah to the Banu al-Mustaliq to collect their charity, and they met him with the charity. He returned and said: 'The Banu al-Mustaliq have gathered against you to fight you.' Qatadah added: 'And they have apostatized from Islam.' So the Messenger of Allah sent Khalid ibn al-Walid to them and commanded him to verify and not to hasten. He set out until he came to them at night, and he sent out his scouts. When they came back, they informed Khalid that they were adhering to Islam, and they heard their adhan and their prayer. When morning came, Khalid went to them and saw what pleased him, so he returned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and informed him of the news, and Allah revealed this verse." Qatadah said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say: 'Verification is from Allah, and haste is from Satan.'"

Similarly, a number of the early generations (al-salaf) mentioned this, among them Ibn Abi Layla, Yazid ibn Ruman, al-Dahhak, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and others, that this verse was revealed concerning al-Walid ibn 'Uqbah. And Allah knows best. [Many exegetes went to this view, but this view requires scrutiny, for the narrations which relate the story are defective, and the best of them, which is the narration of Ahmad from al-Harith ibn Dirar al-Khuza'i, contains an unknown narrator in its chain. Qadi Abu Bakr ibn al-'Arabi denied this story in his book al-'Awasim min al-Qawasim (p. 102), saying: "It has been disputed concerning it. It was said: it was revealed concerning that (i.e., the matter of al-Walid). It was said: it was revealed concerning 'Ali and al-Walid in another incident. It was also said that al-Walid was brought on the day of the Conquest among the group of children to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he wiped their heads and blessed them, all except him, and he said: 'There was perfume on my head,' so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ refrained from touching him. His saying: ﴿And know that among you is the Messenger of Allah﴾ means: know that the Messenger of Allah is in your midst, so honor him, show him reverence, behave courteously with him, and submit to his command, for he knows your interests better than you do, is more compassionate toward you than you are, and his opinion concerning you is more complete than your opinion for yourselves, as Allah said: ﴿The Prophet is closer to the believers than themselves﴾ [al-Ahzab: 6].

Then He clarified [the Exalted] [that their opinion is foolish in comparison to safeguarding their interests], saying: ﴿If he were to obey you in much of the matter, you would be in difficulty﴾, meaning: if he obeyed you in everything you choose, that would lead to your distress and hardship, as Allah said: ﴿And if the truth had followed their desires, the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them would have been corrupted. Rather, We have brought them their reminder, but they, from their reminder, are turning away﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 71].

* *

His saying: ﴿But Allah has endeared to you the faith and made it pleasing in your hearts﴾ means: He made it beloved to your souls and beautiful in your hearts.

Imam Ahmad said: Bahz related to us, 'Ali ibn Mas'adah related to us, Qatadah related to us, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say: "Islam is outward, and faith is in the heart," then he would point with his hand to his chest three times, then say: "Piety is here, piety is here."

﴿And He made disbelief, wickedness, and disobedience hateful to you﴾ means: and He made disbelief and wickedness hateful to you. Wickedness (fusuq) refers to the major sins, and disobedience ('isyan) refers to all sins. This is a gradual progression to the completion of the blessing.

* *

Almighty Allah says, commanding reconciliation between the believers who are fighting one another and transgressing against each other: ﴿And if two groups of the believers fight, then make peace between them﴾. So He calls them believers even while they are fighting. Al-Bukhari and others used this verse as evidence that a person does not leave faith (īmān) because of sin, however grave it may be. As for His saying: ﴿But if one of them transgresses against the other, then fight the one that transgresses until it returns to the command of Allah﴾, that is: until it returns to the command of Allah [in some manuscripts: "to the command of Allah and His Messenger"] and listens to the truth and obeys it. I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I help him when he is oppressed, but how do I help him when he is an oppressor?" He said: "You prevent him from oppressing, and that is your help for him." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 2443].

Imam Ahmad said: Aarim narrated to us, Mu'tamir narrated to us, he said: I heard my father narrate that Anas said: It was said to the Prophet ﷺ, "If only you would go to 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy." A man from the Ansar said: "By Allah, the donkey of the Messenger of Allah is better smelling than you." He said: So men from his people became angry on behalf of 'Abdullah, and each of the two sides was angered by its companions. He said: So there was fighting between them with palm stalks, hands, and sandals. Sa'id ibn Jubayr mentioned that al-Aws and al-Khazraj had fighting between them with palm fronds and sandals, so Allah revealed this verse, and commanded reconciliation between them.

As for His saying: ﴿But if they return, then make peace between them with justice, and act equitably. Indeed, Allah loves those who act equitably﴾, that is: be just between them regarding what some of them caused to others, with equity, which is justice. ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who act equitably﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Muqaddami narrated to us, 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab [in T: "Ibn Abi Hatim narrated with his chain"], from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed the just, in this world, will be upon pulpits of pearl before the Most Merciful, because of their justice in this world."

An-Nasa'i narrated it from Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, from 'Abd al-A'la, with it [in T: "Muslim"] [al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. 5917]. Its chain is good and strong, and its narrators meet the conditions of the Sahih.

Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Yazid narrated to us, Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from 'Amr ibn Aws, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, from the Prophet ﷺ who said: "The just ones with Allah on the Day of Resurrection will be upon pulpits of light, on the right of the Throne, those who are just in their judgment, their families, and what they are responsible for."

Muslim and al-Nasa'i narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, with it [Sahih Muslim no. 1827; Sunan al-Nasa'i 8/321].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿The believers are but brothers﴾, that is: all of them are brothers in religion, as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The Muslim is the brother of the Muslim; he does not wrong him nor forsake him" [narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih no. 2442 and Muslim in his Sahih no. 2580, from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with them both]. In the Sahih: "Allah is in the aid of the servant as long as the servant is in the aid of his brother" [Sahih Muslim no. 2699, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him]. Also in the Sahih: "When a Muslim prays for his brother in his absence, the angel says: Ameen, and for you is the same" [Sahih Muslim no. 2732, from the hadith of Abu al-Darda', may Allah be pleased with him]. The hadiths on this are many. In the Sahih also: "The likeness of the believers in their mutual love, mercy and kindness is like a single body: if one of its limbs complains, the whole body responds to it with wakefulness and fever" [Sahih al-Bukhari].
