As for His saying: ﴿But if they return, then make peace between them with justice, and act equitably. Indeed, Allah loves those who act equitably﴾, that is: be just between them regarding what some of them caused to others, with equity, which is justice. ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who act equitably﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Muqaddami narrated to us, 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab [in T: "Ibn Abi Hatim narrated with his chain"], from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed the just, in this world, will be upon pulpits of pearl before the Most Merciful, because of their justice in this world."

An-Nasa'i narrated it from Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, from 'Abd al-A'la, with it [in T: "Muslim"] [al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. 5917]. Its chain is good and strong, and its narrators meet the conditions of the Sahih.

Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Yazid narrated to us, Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from 'Amr ibn Aws, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, from the Prophet ﷺ who said: "The just ones with Allah on the Day of Resurrection will be upon pulpits of light, on the right of the Throne, those who are just in their judgment, their families, and what they are responsible for."

Muslim and al-Nasa'i narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, with it [Sahih Muslim no. 1827; Sunan al-Nasa'i 8/321].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿The believers are but brothers﴾, that is: all of them are brothers in religion, as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The Muslim is the brother of the Muslim; he does not wrong him nor forsake him" [narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih no. 2442 and Muslim in his Sahih no. 2580, from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with them both]. In the Sahih: "Allah is in the aid of the servant as long as the servant is in the aid of his brother" [Sahih Muslim no. 2699, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him]. Also in the Sahih: "When a Muslim prays for his brother in his absence, the angel says: Ameen, and for you is the same" [Sahih Muslim no. 2732, from the hadith of Abu al-Darda', may Allah be pleased with him]. The hadiths on this are many. In the Sahih also: "The likeness of the believers in their mutual love, mercy and kindness is like a single body: if one of its limbs complains, the whole body responds to it with wakefulness and fever" [Sahih al-Bukhari]. Also in the Sahih: "The believer to the believer is like a building, one part of it strengthening another," and he interlaced his fingers [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 6011 and Sahih Muslim no. 2586, from the hadith of al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, may Allah be pleased with him].

Ahmad said: Ahmad ibn al-Hajjaj narrated to us, 'Abdullah narrated to us, Mus'ab ibn Thabit informed us, Abu Hazim narrated to me, he said: I heard Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi narrate from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ who said: "The believer among the people of faith is like the head in relation to the body: the believer aches for the people of faith as the body aches because of what is in the head" [Musnad (5/340); al-Haythami in al-Majma' (8/187) said: "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih"]. It is narrated uniquely, and there is no harm in its chain.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So make peace between your two brothers﴾, meaning: the two fighting groups, ﴿and fear Allah﴾, that is: in all your affairs, ﴿that you may receive mercy﴾. This is an affirmation from Him, exalted is He, of mercy for those who fear Him.

He, exalted is He, forbids mocking people, which is belittling them and ridiculing them, as it is established in the Sahih from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "Pride is rejecting the truth and looking down on people" (al-Kibr batar al-haqq wa ghamtu al-nas). It is also narrated as "wa ghamtu al-nas" (and despising people). [Sahih Muslim, no. (91), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him).] What is meant by this is belittling them and considering them insignificant, and this is forbidden, for the person being belittled may be greater in worth with Allah and more beloved to Him than the one who mocks him and belittles him. For this reason He said: ﴿O you who have believed, let not a people ridicule [another] people; perhaps they may be better than them, and let not women ridicule [other] women; perhaps they may be better than them﴾. So He explicitly forbade men and linked to it the prohibition for women.

* *

His saying: ﴿And do not defame one another﴾, that is: do not defame people. The one who constantly defames and slanders (al-hammaz al-lammaz) among men is blameworthy and cursed, as He said: ﴿Woe to every scorner and mocker﴾ [al-Humazah: 1]. So al-hamz is by action and al-lamz is by speech, as He said: ﴿a slanderer, going about with gossip﴾ [al-Qalam: 11], meaning he belittles people and defames them, attacking them, and walks among them spreading gossip, which is lamz by words. For this reason He said here: ﴿And do not defame yourselves﴾, just as He said: ﴿And do not kill yourselves﴾ [an-Nisa: 29], meaning that some of you should not kill others.

Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Qatadah, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: ﴿And do not defame yourselves﴾ means: let not some of you find fault with others.

* *

His saying: ﴿And do not insult one another by [offensive] nicknames﴾, that is: do not call one another by nicknames, which are those that the person dislikes to hear.

Imam Ahmad said: Ismail narrated to us, Dawud ibn Abi Hind narrated to us, from al-Sha'bi, who said: Abu Jubayrah ibn al-Dahhak narrated to me, saying: It was revealed about us, concerning the Banu Salamah: ﴿And do not insult one another by nicknames﴾. He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to Madinah and there was not a man among us except that he had two or three names. Whenever one of them was called by one of those names, they would say: "O Messenger of Allah, he becomes angry at this." So it was revealed: ﴿And do not insult one another by nicknames﴾.

Abu Dawud narrated it from Musa ibn Isma'il, from Wuhayb, from Dawud, with the same wording. [Al-Musnad (4/260) and Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (4962). It was also narrated by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. (3268), through the chain of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, and al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih (a sound, reliable hadith)."]

* *

His saying: ﴿How bad is the name of wickedness after faith﴾, that is: how bad is the description and the name of wickedness (fusuq), which is calling one another by nicknames, as the people of the Jahiliyyah (Pre-Islamic Age of Ignorance) used to do, after you had entered Islam and understood it. ﴿And whoever does not repent﴾

that is, from this, ﴿those are the wrongdoers﴾.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 49, verse 12 (part 1 of 3):

Allah the Exalted says, forbidding His believing servants from much suspicion (zann), which is accusing and distrusting one's family, relatives and people when there is no basis for it. Some of it is pure sin, so much of it should be avoided out of caution. We have also related from the Commander of the Believers, 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "Do not think ill of a word that comes from your Muslim brother when you can find a good interpretation for it."[[Narrated by Ahmad in al-Zuhd, as cited in al-Durr al-Manthur (7/565).]]

Ibn Majah, Abu 'Abdullah, said: Abu al-Qasim ibn Abi Damrah Nasr ibn Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Himsi narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: 'Abdullah ibn Abi Qays al-Nadri narrated to us, saying: 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar[[In another version: "Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him."]] narrated to us, saying: "I saw the Prophet (ﷺ) circumambulating the Ka'bah and saying: 'How good you are and how good your fragrance is! How great you are and how great your sanctity is! By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, the sanctity of the believer is greater before Allah than your sanctity: his property, his blood, and that one should think ill of him except in good.'"[[Narrated by Ibn Majah alone through this chain. Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 3932. al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/223): "This chain has some weakness. Nasr ibn Muhammad was declared weak by Abu Hatim, but Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy narrators. The rest of the narrators are trustworthy."]]

Malik said, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Beware of suspicion, for suspicion is the most false of speech. Do not spy (tajassus) and do not pry (tahassus), do not compete for worldly things, do not envy one another, do not hate one another, do not turn away from one another, and be servants of Allah as brothers."

Al-Bukhari related it from 'Abdullah ibn Yusuf, Muslim from Yahya ibn Yahya, and Abu Dawud from al-'Utbi, all three from Malik, with this wording.[[Al-Muwatta' (2/908), Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 6066, and Sahih Muslim, no. 2563.]]

Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah said, from al-Zuhri, from Anas[[Ra]] who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not sever ties, do not turn away from one another, do not hate one another, do not envy one another, and be servants of Allah as brothers. It is not lawful for a Muslim to shun his brother for more than three days."

Muslim and al-Tirmidhi, who authenticated it, related it from the hadith of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah with this wording.[[Sahih Muslim, no. 2559, and Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 1935.]]

Al-Tabarani said: Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah al-Qirmiti al-'Adawi narrated to us, saying: Bakr ibn 'Abd al-Wahhab al-Madani narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Qays al-Ansari narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn Abi al-Rijal narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather Harithah ibn al-Nu'man, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "Three things will afflict my Ummah: tiyarah (superstitious belief in omens), envy, and evil suspicion." A man said: "What will remove them, O Messenger of Allah, for those who have them?" He said: "When you envy, seek forgiveness from Allah; when you suspect, do not confirm it; and when you feel tiyarah, proceed (and do not let it influence you)."[[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (3/228). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/78): "It contains Isma'il ibn Qays al-Ansari, who is weak."]]

Abu Dawud said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Zayd, who said: Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, was brought a man, and it was said to him: "This is so-and-so, whose beard drips with wine." 'Abdullah said: "We have been forbidden from spying (tajassus), but if something becomes apparent to us, we will act upon it."[[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 4890.]]

Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned in his narration that this man was al-Walid ibn 'Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt.[[This was because people had spoken much about al-Walid ibn 'Uqbah. Ibn Mas'ud was in charge of the treasury during al-Walid ibn 'Uqbah's governorship in the time of 'Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him. The story of al-Walid being flogged for drinking wine is well known and is in the two Sahihs.]]

Imam Ahmad said: Hashim narrated to us, saying: Layth narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Nashit al-Khawlani, from Ka'b ibn 'Alqamah, from Abu al-Haytham, from Dukhayn, the scribe of 'Uqbah, who said: I said to 'Uqbah: "We have neighbors who drink wine, and I will call the police (shurtah) on them so that they seize them." He said: "Do not do that, but admonish them and threaten them." So he did, but they did not desist. Dukhayn came back and said: "I admonished them and they did not desist, and I will call the police on them so that they seize them." He said: "Do not do that, but admonish them and threaten them." So he did, but they did not desist. Dukhayn came back and said: "I admonished them and they did not desist, and I will call the police so that they seize them." 'Uqbah said to him: "Woe to you! Do not do that, for I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Whoever conceals the faults (awrah) of a believer, it is as if he has revived a buried girl from her grave.'"

Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i related it from the hadith of Layth ibn Sa'd, with similar wording.[[Al-Musnad (4/153), Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 4892, and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. 7283.]]

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Thawr, from Rashid ibn Sa'd, from Mu'awiyah, who said: "I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: 'If you pursue the faults of people, you will corrupt them,' or: 'You almost corrupt them.'" Abu al-Darda' said: "It is a word that Mu'awiyah heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), by which Allah benefited him." Abu Dawud alone related it from the hadith of al-Thawri, with this wording.[[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 4888.]]

Abu Dawud also said: Sa'id ibn 'Amr al-Hadrami narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, saying: Damdam ibn Zur'ah narrated to us, from Shurayh ibn 'Ubayd, from Jubayr ibn Nufayr, Kathir ibn Murrah, 'Amr ibn al-Aswad, al-Miqdam ibn Ma'dikarib, and Abu Umamah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "If the ruler seeks out doubts about the people, he corrupts them."[[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 4889.]]

[And His saying]: ﴿And do not spy﴾, meaning: on one another. Tajassus is generally used for evil, and from it comes the word jasus (spy). Tahassus is generally used for good, as Allah the Exalted related about Ya'qub, peace be upon him, when he said: ﴿O my sons, go and search for news of Yusuf and his brother, and do not despair of the mercy of Allah﴾ [Yusuf: 87]. Either of them may be used for evil, as is established in the Sahih, where the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not spy (tajassus), do not pry (tahassus), do not hate one another, do not turn away from one another, and be servants of Allah as brothers."[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 2442.]]

Al-Awza'i said: Tajassus is searching for a thing, and tahassus is listening to the conversation of a people who dislike it, or eavesdropping at their doors. Tadabbur is severance. Ibn Abi Hatim related it.

* *

His saying: ﴿And let not some of you backbite others﴾ contains a prohibition of backbiting (ghibah). The Lawgiver (al-Shari') explained it, as came in the hadith related by Abu Dawud: al-Qa'nabi narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Aziz ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from al-'Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurayrah[[May Allah be pleased with him.]], who said: It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is ghibah?" He said: "Your mention of your brother in a way he dislikes." It was said: "What if what I say is true of my brother?" He said: "If what you say is in him, then you have backbitten him, and if it is not in him, then you have slandered him (bahtah)."

al-Tirmidhi related it from Qutaybah, from al-Darawardi, with this wording,[[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 4874, and Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 1935.]] and said: "Hasan sahih." Ibn Jarir related it from Bundar, from Ghundar, from Shu'bah, from al-'Ala'.[[Tafsir al-Tabari (26/86).]] This was also the view of Ibn 'Umar, Masruq, Qatadah, Abu Ishaq, and Mu'awiyah ibn Qurrah.

Abu Dawud said: Musaddad narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, from Sufyan, saying: 'Ali ibn al-Aqmar narrated to me, from Abu Hudhayfah, from 'A'ishah, who said: "I said to the Prophet (ﷺ): 'Sufficient for you from Safiyyah is such-and-such!' (Someone other than Musaddad said: she meant that she was short.) He said: 'You have said a word which, if it were mixed with the water of the sea, would have altered it.'" She said: "I imitated someone for him, and he said: 'I would not like to imitate a person, even if I were given such-and-such.'"

al-Tirmidhi related it from the hadith of Yahya al-Qattan, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, and Waki', all three from Sufyan al-Thawri, from 'Ali ibn al-Aqmar, from Abu Hudhayfah Salamah ibn Suhaybah al-Arhabi, from 'A'ishah, with this wording, and said: "Hasan sahih."[[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 4875, and Sunan al-Tirmidhi, nos. 2502, 2503.]]

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Abi al-Shawarib narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad narrated to us, saying: Sulayman al-Shaybani narrated to us, saying: Hassan ibn al-Mukhariq narrated to us, that a woman entered upon 'A'ishah, and when she stood to leave, 'A'ishah gestured with her hand toward the Prophet (ﷺ), meaning that she was short. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "You have backbitten her."[[Tafsir al-Tabari (26/87).]]

Ghibah is forbidden by consensus (ijma'). Excluded from this is only what has a greater benefit, as in criticism and validation of narrators (jarh wa ta'dil), in giving sincere advice (nasihah), and like the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) when that wicked man sought permission to enter upon him: "Admit him, for he is a bad brother of the clan."[[Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 3132, from the hadith of 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her.]] Also like his saying to Fatimah bint Qays, when Mu'awiyah and Abu al-Jahm had proposed to her: "As for Mu'awiyah, he is a poor man with no property; as for Abu al-Jahm, he does not put down his staff from his shoulder."[[Related by Muslim in his Sahih, no. 1480.]] And whatever follows this course. Beyond these cases, it remains strictly forbidden, and a severe warning has come concerning it. For this reason Allah the Exalted likened it to eating the flesh of a dead human being, as He said: ﴿Would any of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother? You would detest it﴾. That is, just as you dislike this by nature, dislike that by law, for its punishment is more severe than this, and this is a deterrent from it and a warning against it. As the Prophet (ﷺ) said about one who takes back his gift: "Like a dog that vomits and then returns to its vomit." He also said: "We do not have a bad example." It is established in the Sahihs, the sound (hisan) collections and the Musnads through more than one route that he (ﷺ), in the Farewell Sermon (khutbat hajjat al-wada'), said: "Indeed your blood, your property and your honor are sacred to you, just as the sanctity of this day, in this month, in this land of yours."[[Related by Muslim in his Sahih, no. 1218, from the hadith of Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

Abu Dawud said: Wasil ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Asbat ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Sa'd, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Every Muslim is sacred to another Muslim: his property, his honor and his blood. It is enough evil for a person to despise his Muslim brother."

al-Tirmidhi related it[[In another version: "al-Tirmidhi related it and graded it hasan."]] from 'Ubayd ibn Asbat ibn Muhammad, from his father, with this wording,[[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 4882, and Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 1927.]] and said: "Hasan gharib."

'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah[[In another version: "Abu Dawud related it."]] narrated to us, saying: al-Aswad ibn 'Amir narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Sa'id ibn 'Abd Allah[[In another version: "'Ubayd Allah."]] ibn Jurayj, from Abu Barzah al-Aslami, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "O assembly of those who have believed with their tongues while faith has not entered their hearts! Do not backbite the Muslims, and do not pursue their faults, for whoever pursues their faults, Allah will pursue his fault, and whoever Allah pursues for his fault, He will expose him in his own house."

Abu Dawud alone narrated it. [Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 4880.] It has also been narrated from the hadith of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib. The Hafiz Abu Ya'la said in his Musnad (a collection arranged by companion narrator): Ibrahim ibn Dinar related to us, Mus'ab ibn Sallam related to us, from Hamzah ibn Habib al-Zayyat, from Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) addressed us until he made the young women in their houses hear him, or he said: in their private chambers. He said: "O assembly of those who have believed with their tongues, do not backbite Muslims and do not seek out their faults. Whoever seeks out the faults of his brother, Allah will seek out his fault, and whoever Allah seeks out his fault for, He will expose him, even within his house." [Musnad Abi Ya'la (3/237). al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/93): "Its narrators are trustworthy."]

Another route from Ibn 'Umar: Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Isma'ili said: 'Abd Allah ibn Najiyah informed us, Yahya ibn Aktham related to us, al-Fadl ibn Musa al-Shaybani related to us, from al-Husayn ibn Waqid, from Awfa ibn Dalham, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O assembly of those who have believed with their tongues while faith has not reached their hearts, do not backbite Muslims and do not seek out their faults. Whoever seeks out the faults of Muslims, Allah will seek out his fault, and whoever Allah seeks out his fault for, He will expose him, even within his riding-saddle." He said: Ibn 'Umar once looked at the Ka'bah and said: "How great you are, and how great your sanctity is! Yet the believer has greater sanctity with Allah than you." [Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in his Sunan (no. 2032) through al-Fadl ibn Musa, and said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith. We only know it from the hadith of al-Husayn ibn Waqid."]

Abu Dawud said: Haywah ibn Shurayh related to us, Baqiyyah related to us, from Ibn Thawban, from his father, from Makhul, from Waqqas ibn Rabi'ah, from al-Mustawrid, that he related to him that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever eats a meal at the expense of a Muslim man, Allah will feed him the like of it in Jahannam. Whoever clothes himself with a garment at the expense of a Muslim man, Allah will clothe him with the like of it in Jahannam. And whoever stands on behalf of a man in a position of showing off and seeking reputation, Allah will stand him in a position of showing off and seeking reputation on the Day of Resurrection." Abu Dawud alone narrated it. [Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 4881.]

Ibn Musaffa related to us: Baqiyyah and Abu al-Mughirah related to us, both saying: Safwan related to us, Rashid ibn Sa'd and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr related to me, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When I was taken up on the Night Journey, I passed by a people who had nails of copper, scratching their faces and chests. I said: 'Who are these, O Jibril?' He said: 'These are the ones who eat the flesh of people and fall into their honour.'"

Abu Dawud alone narrated it. Likewise Imam Ahmad narrated it from Abu al-Mughirah 'Abd al-Quddus ibn al-Hajjaj al-Shami, with the same chain. [Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 4878; al-Musnad (3/224).]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us, Ahmad ibn 'Abdah related to us, Abu 'Abd al-Samad 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn 'Abd al-Samad al-'Ammi related to us, Abu Harun al-'Abdi related to us, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri [may Allah be pleased with him], who said: We said: "O Messenger of Allah, tell us what you saw on the night you were taken on the Night Journey?" ... He said: "Then I was taken to a great number of Allah's creatures, men and women, over whom were appointed men who would target the side of one of them and cut from it a piece the size of a sandal, then place it in the mouth of that person. It would be said to him: 'Eat as you have eaten,' and he would find the eating of it to be death, O Muhammad. He would find death if he were compelled to it." I said: "O Jibril, who are these?" He said: "These are the backbiters and slanderers, the people of tale-bearing." Then it is said: ﴿Would any of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother? You would hate it.﴾ And he is compelled to eat his flesh.

Thus he narrated this hadith. We have quoted it in full at the beginning of the tafsir of Surat Subhan, and to Allah belongs all praise. [At the first verse.]

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said in his Musnad: al-Rabi' related to us, from Yazid, from Anas, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded the people to fast one day, and no one was to break the fast until he gave permission. The people fasted, and when evening came, a man would come to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and say: "I have been fasting since the morning, so permit me to break my fast." He would permit him. Another man would come and say the same, and he would permit him, until a man came and said: "O Messenger of Allah, two young women from your family have been fasting since the morning, so permit them to break their fast." He turned away from him, then he repeated it, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "They have not fasted. How can one fast who has been eating the flesh of people? Go, and command them, if they were fasting, to vomit." They did so, and each of them vomited a clot of blood, a clot each. He came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If they had died while they were in that state, the Fire would have consumed them." [Musnad al-Tayalisi (no. 2107).]

Its chain is weak, and its text is gharib (rare). The Hafiz al-Bayhaqi narrated it from the hadith of Yazid ibn Harun: Sulayman al-Taymi related to us, saying: I heard a man narrating in the assembly of Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, from 'Ubayd, the freedman of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that two women fasted during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and a man came to the Messenger of Allah and said: "O Messenger of Allah, there are two women here who have fasted, and they are nearly dying of thirst." I think he said: "at midday." He turned away from him, or remained silent, then he said: "O Prophet of Allah, they have, by Allah, died or are nearly dying." He said: "Call them." They came, and a bowl or a cup was brought. He said to one of them: "Vomit." She vomited pus, blood and discharge until she had vomited half the bowl. Then he said to the other: "Vomit." She vomited pus, blood, discharge, flesh, fresh blood and other matter until she filled the bowl. He said: "These two fasted from what Allah had made lawful for them, and broke their fast with what Allah had made unlawful for them. One of them sat with the other, and they began to eat the flesh of people."

Likewise Imam Ahmad narrated it from Yazid ibn Harun and Ibn Abi 'Adiy, both from Sulayman ibn Tarkhan al-Taymi, with the same or similar wording. [Al-Musnad (5/431); Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated it in al-Samt (no. 171) through Yazid ibn Harun from Sulayman al-Taymi.] Then he also narrated it from the hadith of Musaddad, from Yahya al-Qattan, from 'Uthman ibn Ghiyath, who said: a man, whom I think was in the circle of Abu 'Uthman, told me, from Sa'd, the freedman of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that they were commanded to fast. A man came at midday and said: "O Messenger of Allah, so-and-so and so-and-so have reached the limit of exhaustion." He turned away from him twice or three times, then said: "Call them." A bowl or cup was brought, and he said to one of them: "Vomit." She vomited flesh, fresh blood and pus. He said the same to the other, then said: "These two fasted from what Allah had made lawful for them, and broke their fast with what Allah had made unlawful for them. One came to the other, and they kept on eating the flesh of people until their insides were filled with pus." [Al-Musnad (5/431).]

Al-Bayhaqi said: Thus he said "from Sa'd," but the first, which is 'Ubayd, is more sound.

The Hafiz Abu Ya'la said: 'Amr ibn al-Dahhak ibn Makhlad related to us, my father Abu 'Asim related to us, Ibn Jurayj related to us, Abu al-Zubayr informed me, from a paternal cousin of Abu Hurayrah, that Ma'iz came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have committed adultery." He turned away from him, and he said it four times. When it was the fifth time, he said: "Did you commit adultery?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Do you know what adultery is?" He said: "Yes, I had unlawful relations with her, as a man has lawful relations with his wife." He said: "What do you intend by this statement?" He said: "I want you to purify me." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Did you put that part of yours into that part of hers, as the kohl-stick disappears into the kohl-pot and the rope into the well?" He said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He commanded that he be stoned, and he was stoned. The Prophet (ﷺ) heard two men, one saying to the other: "Did you not see this one whom Allah had covered, but his own soul did not leave him alone until he was stoned like a dog?" Then the Prophet (ﷺ) went on until he passed by the carcass of a donkey and said: "Where are so-and-so and so-and-so? Dismount and eat from the carcass of this donkey." They both said: "May Allah forgive you, O Messenger of Allah! Would this be eaten?" He said: "What you two have taken from your brother just now is more eating than this. By Him in whose hand my soul is, he is now in the rivers of Paradise, immersing himself in them."

[Musnad Abi Ya'la (6/524). al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Sunan al-Kubra (8/227) through 'Amr ibn al-Dahhak; Abu Dawud narrated it in his Sunan (no. 4429) through al-Dahhak.] Its chain is sahih.

Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Samad related to us, my father related to me, Wasil, the freedman of Ibn 'Uyaynah, related to us, Khalid ibn 'Urfutah related to me, from Talhah ibn Nafi', from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: We were with the Prophet (ﷺ) when a foul smell of a putrid carcass rose up. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do you know what this smell is? This is the smell of those who backbite the believers." [Al-Musnad (3/351). al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/91): "Its narrators are trustworthy."]

Another route: 'Abd ibn Humayd said in his Musnad: Ibrahim ibn al-Ash'ath related to us, al-Fudayl ibn 'Iyad related to us, from Sulayman, from Abu Sufyan, who is Talhah ibn Nafi', from Jabir, who said: We were with the Prophet (ﷺ) on a journey when a foul, putrid wind blew. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "A group of hypocrites backbit some Muslims, and because of that this wind was sent." Perhaps he said: "Because of that this wind blew." [Al-Muntakhab (no. 1026).]

Al-Suddi said, regarding His words ﴿Would any of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother?﴾: He claimed that Salman al-Farisi was with two men among the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) on a journey, serving them, lightening their load, and taking some of their food. One day the people set out, and Salman remained sleeping and did not travel with them. His two companions began speaking to him but found him unresponsive. They struck the tent and said: "What does Sulayman (or this slave) want except this: to come to ready food and a pitched tent!" When Salman came, they sent him to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to ask for some condiment for them. He set off and came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with a bowl of his own and said: "O Messenger of Allah, my companions have sent me to ask you for condiment, if you have any?" He said: "What do your companions do with condiment? They have already eaten condiment." Salman returned to inform them of the words of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). They both set out until they came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "No, by Him who sent you with the truth, we have not eaten any food since we arrived." He said: "You two have eaten condiment with Salman through your words."

He said: And it was revealed: ﴿Would any of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother?﴾ Indeed, he was sleeping. [Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it in his tafsir, as in al-Durr al-Manthur (7/570).]

Ibn Kathir's commentary on surah 49, verse 12 (part 3 of 3):

Al-Hafiz al-Diya' al-Maqdisi related in his book "al-Mukhtarah," through the chain of Habban ibn Hilal, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Thabit, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Arabs used to serve one another during journeys, and with Abu Bakr and Umar there was a man who served them both. They fell asleep, then woke up and no food had been prepared for them. They said: "This man is truly a sleeper." So they woke him and said to him: "Go to the Messenger of Allah and say to him: Abu Bakr and Umar send you their greetings and ask you for some food (to eat with bread)."

He said: "They have already had their food (idtamaa)." They came and said: "O Messenger of Allah, with what have we had our food?" He said: "With the flesh of your brother. By Him in whose hand is my soul, I can indeed see its flesh between your teeth." They said: "Ask forgiveness for us, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Tell him to ask forgiveness for you both." [[al-Mukhtarah, no. (1697).]]

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la said: Al-Hakam ibn Musa related to us, Muhammad ibn Muslim related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from his paternal uncle Musa ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever eats the flesh of his brother in this world, his flesh will be brought before him in the Hereafter, and it will be said to him: Eat it dead as you ate it alive." He said: "So he will eat it, grimacing and screaming." This is very strange (gharib jiddan). [[Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat, no. (4961), "Majma' al-Bahrayn," through the chain of Muhammad ibn Salamah from Muhammad ibn Ishaq. He said: No one narrated it from Ibn Ishaq except Muhammad ibn Salamah, and here it appears as "Muhammad ibn Muslim," which I think is a scribal error (tashif), but I cannot be certain. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/92): "It contains Ibn Ishaq, who is a mudallis, and one whom I do not know."]]

* *

His words, ﴿And fear Allah﴾, mean: regarding what He has commanded you and forbidden you, so be watchful of Him in this and fear Him. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Accepting of repentance and Merciful﴾, meaning: He accepts the repentance of whoever repents to Him, and is merciful to whoever returns to Him and relies upon Him.

The majority of scholars said: The way for one who has backbitten people to repent is that he must cease this practice and resolve never to return to it. Is it a condition that he feel remorse over what has passed? There is disagreement on this. And he must seek to be absolved by the person he backbit. Others said: It is not a condition that he seek that person's absolution, for if he informs him of it, it may hurt him more than if he did not know what he had said. Rather, his way (of repentance) is to praise that person for what is good in him in the gatherings where he used to disparage him, and to defend him against backbiting according to his ability and capacity, so that this will be in exchange for that. As Imam Ahmad related:

Ahmad ibn al-Hajjaj related to us, Abdullah informed us, Yahya ibn Ayyub informed us, from Abdullah ibn Sulayman, that Isma'il ibn Yahya al-Ma'afiri informed him that Sahl ibn Mu'adh ibn Anas al-Juhani informed him, from his father, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever protects a believer from a hypocrite who disparages him, Allah will send to him an angel who will protect his flesh from the Fire of Hell on the Day of Resurrection. And whoever attacks a believer with something, intending to disgrace him, Allah will detain him on the bridge of Hell until he emerges from what he said." Abu Dawud also related it in similar form from the narration of Abdullah (i.e., Ibn al-Mubarak) through the same chain. [[Musnad (3/441) and Sunan Abi Dawud no. (4883).]]

Abu Dawud also said: Ishaq ibn al-Sabbah related to us, Ibn Abi Maryam related to us, al-Layth informed us, Yahya ibn Sulaym related to me that he heard Isma'il ibn Bashir say: I heard Jabir ibn Abdullah and Abu Talhah ibn Sahl al-Ansari say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no person who forsakes a Muslim man in a situation where his sanctity is violated and his honor is belittled, except that Allah will forsake him in situations where he loves to be helped. And there is no person who helps a Muslim man in a situation where his honor is belittled and his sanctity is violated, except that Allah will help him in situations where he loves to be helped." Abu Dawud alone narrated it. [[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (4884).]]

The Most High says, informing mankind that He created them from a single soul, and made from it its mate, who were Adam and Eve, and made them into *shu'ub* (nations), which is more general than *qaba'il* (tribes). After the tribes there are other levels, such as the *fasa'il* (clans), the *'ashair* (kin groups), the *'amair* (extended families), and the *afkhad* (branches), and other than these.

It has been said: by *shu'ub* is meant the lineages of the *'ajam* (non-Arabs), and by *qaba'il* the lineages of the *'Arab*, just as the *asbat* (tribes) are the lineages of the Children of Israel. I have summarised this in a separate introduction, compiled from the book *al-Inbah* (*Al-Inbah*) by Abu 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Barr, and from the book *al-Qasd wal-Umam fi Ma'rifat Ansab al-'Arab wal-'Ajam* (*The Intent and the Nations in Knowing the Genealogies of the Arabs and the Non-Arabs*). All people are equal in nobility, by their clay-based descent from Adam and Eve; they differ only in religious matters, which are obedience to Allah and following His Messenger (ﷺ). For this reason, after forbidding backbiting and the belittling of some people by others, and drawing attention to their equality in humanity, the Most High said: ﴿O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you into nations and tribes that you may know one another.﴾ That is, so that acquaintance may take place among them, each returning to his own tribe.

Mujahid said, regarding His words ﴿that you may know one another﴾, that it is as one says: "So-and-so, son of so-and-so, from such-and-such," meaning from such-and-such a tribe.

Sufyan al-Thawri said: The Himyar used to trace their lineage to their *makhalif* (districts), while the Arabs of the Hijaz used to trace their lineage to their tribes.

Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi narrated: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated to us, 'Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Isa al-Thaqafi, from Yazid, the client of al-Mun'abith, from Abu Hurairah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Learn from your genealogies what you need in order to keep your ties of kinship, for keeping ties of kinship is a source of love among family, an increase of wealth, and an extension of one's life." Then he said: It is *gharib* (a narration with a single line of transmission); we do not know it except through this route.

* *

His words ﴿Indeed, the most honourable of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you﴾ mean: you are only distinguished before Allah by piety, not by lineage. Hadiths to this effect have been reported from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ):

Al-Bukhari, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Muhammad ibn Salam narrated to us, 'Abdah narrated to us, from 'Ubaid Allah, from Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id, from Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked: "Who are the most honourable people?" He said: "The most honourable of them in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of them." They said: "We are not asking you about this." He said: "Then the most honourable people is Yusuf, the Prophet of Allah, son of the Prophet of Allah, son of the Friend of Allah." They said: "We are not asking you about this." He said: "Then are you asking me about the mines of the Arabs?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Then the best of you in the Jahiliyyah are the best of you in Islam, when they gain understanding."

Al-Bukhari narrated this in more than one place, through several routes from 'Abdah ibn Sulaiman. An-Nasa'i narrated it in his *Tafsir* from the hadith of 'Ubaid Allah, who is Ibn 'Umar al-'Umari, with the same wording.

Another hadith: Muslim, may Allah have mercy on him, said: 'Amr al-Naqid narrated to us, Kathir ibn Hisham narrated to us, Ja'far ibn Burqan narrated to us, from Yazid ibn al-Asamm, from Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah does not look at your forms or your wealth, but He looks at your hearts and your deeds."

Ibn Majah narrated it from Ahmad ibn Sinan, from Kathir ibn Hisham, with the same chain.

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, from Abu Hilal, from Bakr, from Abu Dharr, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "Look, you are not better than a red man nor a black man, except that you surpass him in piety." Ahmad alone narrated it.

Another hadith: The memorizer Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Abu 'Ubaidah 'Abd al-Warith ibn Ibrahim al-'Askari narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Amr ibn Jabalah narrated to us, 'Ubaid ibn Hunain al-Ta'i narrated to us, I heard Muhammad ibn Habib ibn Khirash al-'Asri narrating from his father, that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "The Muslims are brothers; none has any superiority over another except by piety."

Another hadith: Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said in his *Musnad*: Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Kufi narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn al-Husain narrated to us, Qais, that is Ibn al-Rabi', narrated to us, from Shabib ibn Gharqada, from al-Mustazil ibn Husain, from Hudhaifah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "You are all the children of Adam, and Adam was created from dust. Let people stop boasting of their fathers, or they will be more contemptible in the sight of Allah than the dung-beetles."

Then he said: We do not know it from Hudhaifah except through this route.

Another hadith: Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Rabi' ibn Sulaiman narrated to us, Asad ibn Musa narrated to us, Yahya ibn Zakariyya al-Qattan narrated to us, Musa ibn 'Ubaidah narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Dinar, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: On the day of the Conquest of Makkah, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) circled the Ka'bah on his she-camel al-Qaswa, touching the corners with a staff in his hand. He did not find a place for her to kneel in the mosque, until he dismounted with the help of the men's hands, and she was led out to the valley of the watercourse, where she knelt. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) addressed them while on his mount, praised Allah and extolled Him as is fitting for Him, then said: "O people, Allah has removed from you the arrogance of the Jahiliyyah and its pride in ancestors. People are of two kinds: a righteous, pious, noble person who is honoured by Allah, and a wicked, miserable person who is despised by Allah. Indeed Allah says: ﴿O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you into nations and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most honourable of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you. Indeed Allah is Knowing and Acquainted.﴾" Then he said: "I say this statement of mine and I seek forgiveness from Allah for me and for you."

Thus did 'Abd ibn Humaid narrate it, from Abu 'Asim al-Dahhak ibn Makhlad, from Musa ibn 'Ubaidah, with the same chain.

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, from al-Harith ibn Yazid, from 'Ali ibn Rabah, from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed these lineages of yours are not a cause of disgrace for anyone. You are all the children of Adam; the measure is full but not packed. No one has any superiority over another except through religion and piety, and it is enough for a man to be vulgar, miserly and obscene."

Ibn Jarir narrated it from Yunus, from Ibn Wahb, from Ibn Lahi'ah, with the same chain. Its wording is: "The people are for Adam and Eve; the measure is full but they have not filled it. Indeed Allah will not ask you on the Day of Resurrection about your lineages or your ancestries. Indeed the most honourable of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you."

It is not found in any of the Six Books through this route.

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Malik narrated to us, Sharik narrated to us, from Simak, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umairah, husband of Durrah bint Abi Lahab, from Durrah bint Abi Lahab, who said: A man stood before the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was on the pulpit and said: "O Messenger of Allah, who is the best of people?" He (ﷺ) said: "The best of people is the one who recites the most, the most God-fearing of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, the one who most enjoins what is right, forbids what is wrong, and keeps the ties of kinship the most."

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Hasan narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, Abu al-Aswad narrated to us, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from 'A'ishah, who said: Nothing of this world ever pleased the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and no one ever pleased him, except one who is pious. Ahmad alone narrated it, may Allah have mercy on him.

* *

His words ﴿Indeed Allah is Knowing and Acquainted﴾ mean: He is Knowing of you and Acquainted with your affairs. So He guides whom He wills, leads astray whom He wills, shows mercy to whom He wills, punishes whom He wills, and favours whom He wills over whom He wills, and He is the Wise, the Knowing, the Acquainted in all of that. Scholars who held that equality (*kafa'ah*) in marriage is not a condition, and that nothing other than religion is required, have used this noble verse and these noble hadiths as evidence, based on His words ﴿Indeed the most honourable of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you﴾. Others held to other evidences mentioned in the books of jurisprudence. We have mentioned some of that in our book *al-Ahkam*, and to Allah belongs praise and grace. Al-Tabarani narrated from 'Abd al-Rahman that he heard a man from the Banu Hashim saying: "I am the closest of people to the Messenger of Allah." He said: "Someone other than you is closer to him than you are, and his lineage is yours."

Allah the Exalted says, rebuking the Bedouin Arabs who, at the very beginning of their entry into Islam, claimed for themselves the rank of faith while faith had not yet settled in their hearts: ﴿The Bedouins say, "We have believed." Say, "You have not [yet] believed; but say, 'We have submitted,' for faith has not yet entered your hearts."﴾. From this noble verse it is derived that faith (īmān) is more specific than submission (islām), as is the position of the People of the Sunnah and the Jama'ah (Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah). This is indicated by the hadith of Jibril, upon him be peace, when he asked about Islam, then about faith, then about excellence (iḥsān), progressing from the more general to the more specific, and then to what is more specific than that.

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Amir ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave to some men and did not give anything to one man among them. Sa'd said: "O Messenger of Allah, you gave to so-and-so and so-and-so, and you did not give so-and-so anything, yet he is a believer (mu'min)?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Or a Muslim (muslim)," and Sa'd repeated it three times, while the Prophet (ﷺ) kept saying: "Or a Muslim." Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I give to men and leave out the one who is dearer to me than them, not giving him anything, fearing that they will be thrown face-first into the Fire."

Both al-Bukhari and Muslim recorded it in their Sahihs through the hadith of al-Zuhri with this chain.

The Prophet (ﷺ) distinguished between the Muslim and the believer, which indicates that faith is more specific than submission. We have established this with its evidences at the beginning of the explanation of the Book of Faith in Sahih al-Bukhari, and to Allah belongs all praise and grace. This also indicates that that man was a Muslim and not a hypocrite, since he withheld from him the gift and left him to what he was in of Islam. This shows that the Bedouins mentioned in this verse are not hypocrites; rather they are Muslims whose faith had not yet become firmly established in their hearts, so they claimed for themselves a rank higher than what they had reached, and so they were disciplined for that. This is the meaning of the statement of Ibn Abbas, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, and Qatadah, and Ibn Jarir chose it.

We have said this because al-Bukhari, may Allah have mercy on him, held that these were hypocrites who displayed faith, but they were not so. It has been related from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, and Ibn Zayd that they said regarding His words ﴿but say, "We have submitted"﴾ that it means: they submitted out of fear of being killed and taken captive. Mujahid said: It was revealed concerning the Banu Asad ibn Khuzaymah. Qatadah said: It was revealed concerning a people who regarded their faith as a favor upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

The correct view is the first: that they were a people who claimed for themselves the rank of faith, which had not yet been attained by them, so they were disciplined and informed that they had not yet reached it. Had they been hypocrites, they would have been rebuked and exposed, as the hypocrites are mentioned in Surah Bara'ah. Rather, these were addressed in a disciplinary manner: ﴿Say, "You have not [yet] believed; but say, 'We have submitted,' for faith has not yet entered your hearts."﴾, meaning: you have not yet reached the reality of faith.

Then He said: ﴿And if you obey Allah and His Messenger, He will not deprive you of [anything] from your deeds﴾, meaning: He will not diminish anything from your rewards, like His words: ﴿And We did not deprive them of anything of their deeds﴾ [al-Tur: 21].

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, meaning: toward whoever repents to Him and turns back to Him.

And His saying: ﴿The believers are only those﴾, meaning: the believers in the complete sense ﴿who believe in Allah and His Messenger and then do not doubt﴾, meaning: they do not waver or vacillate, but remain steadfast in one state, which is pure affirmation, ﴿and strive with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah﴾, meaning: they expend their souls and the precious parts of their wealth in obedience to Allah and seeking His pleasure. ﴿Those are the truthful﴾, meaning: in their statement when they say, "We are believers," unlike some of the Bedouins who have with them of religion only the outward word.

Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Ghaylan narrated to us, Rishdin narrated to us, Amr ibn al-Harith narrated to me, from Abu al-Samh, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The believers in this world are in three categories: those who believe in Allah and His Messenger, then do not doubt, and strive with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah; and the one whom people trust with their wealth and their lives; then the one who, when he is faced with a temptation, leaves it for the sake of Allah, Mighty and Majestic." (Musnad 3/8; its chain contains Ibn Abi al-Samh from Abu al-Haytham, who is weak.)

And His saying: ﴿Say, "Do you inform Allah of your religion?"﴾, meaning: do you inform Him of what is in your hearts? ﴿And Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth﴾, meaning: nothing is hidden from Him on earth or in heaven, nor anything smaller than that or greater. ﴿And Allah is Knowing of all things.﴾

Then He said: ﴿They consider it a favor to you that they have accepted Islam﴾, meaning: the Bedouins who count their Islam, their following, and their support of the Messenger as a favor. Allah responds to them: ﴿Say, "Do not consider your Islam a favor to me. Rather, Allah has conferred favor upon you that He guided you to faith, if you are truthful."﴾, meaning: in your claim. Just as the Prophet (ﷺ) said to the Ansar on the day of Hunayn: "O assembly of the Ansar, did I not find you astray and Allah guided you through me? And you were divided and Allah united you through me? And you were in need and Allah enriched you through me?" Whenever he said something, they replied: "Allah and His Messenger are most gracious." (Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 4330, from Abdullah ibn Zayd ibn Asim, may Allah be pleased with him.)

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Ibrahim ibn Sa'id al-Jawhari narrated to us, Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Umawi narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Awn, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: The Banu Asad came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, we have embraced Islam, while the Arabs fought you and you did not fight them." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, their understanding is little, and Satan speaks through their tongues." And this verse was revealed: ﴿They consider it a favor to you that they have accepted Islam. Say, "Do not consider your Islam a favor to me. Rather, Allah has conferred favor upon you that He guided you to faith, if you are truthful."﴾

Then he said: We do not know it to be narrated except through this route, and we do not know that Abu Awn Muhammad ibn Ubayd Allah narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr anything other than this hadith. (Also related by al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. 11519, through the route of Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Umawi.)

Then He repeated the information of His knowledge of all existing things and His seeing of the deeds of creatures, saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is Seeing of what you do.﴾

End of the tafsir of Surat al-Hujurat, and to Allah belongs all praise and grace.

Allah the Exalted says, rebuking the Bedouin Arabs who, at the very beginning of their entry into Islam, claimed for themselves the rank of faith while faith had not yet settled in their hearts: ﴿The Bedouins say, "We have believed." Say, "You have not [yet] believed; but say, 'We have submitted,' for faith has not yet entered your hearts."﴾. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Ibrahim ibn Sa'id al-Jawhari narrated to us, Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Umawi narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Awn, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: The Banu Asad came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, we have embraced Islam, while the Arabs fought you and you did not fight them." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, their understanding is little, and Satan speaks through their tongues." And this verse was revealed: ﴿They consider it a favor to you that they have accepted Islam. Say, "Do not consider your Islam a favor to me. Rather, Allah has conferred favor upon you that He guided you to faith, if you are truthful."﴾

Then he said: We do not know it to be narrated except through this route, and we do not know that Abu Awn Muhammad ibn Ubayd Allah narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr anything other than this hadith. (Also related by al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. 11519, through the route of Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Umawi.)

Then He repeated the information of His knowledge of all existing things and His seeing of the deeds of creatures, saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is Seeing of what you do.﴾

End of the tafsir of Surat al-Hujurat, and to Allah belongs all praise and grace.
